flashcards.back: A disturbance that carries energy from place to place without carrying matter with it: the particles vibrate in place while the energy moves on.
A wave whose vibration is across the direction of travel, like light: a particle on the wave bobs up and down while the wave races sideways.
A wave whose vibration is along the direction of travel, like sound: the particles bunch together and spread apart as the wave passes.
How many full waves pass a point each second, measured in hertz (Hz): a frequency of 170 Hz means 170 waves per second.
The length of one full wave, from one crest to the next, measured in metres: the sound wave in this lesson has a wavelength of 2 m.

A thunderclap feels so powerful that it seems to arrive before the flash. Light is far faster: the lightning flash arrives first and the thunder follows. That is why, in a storm, you always see the flash before you hear the thunder.
Wrong - light is far faster, so the flash arrives first and the thunder follows
flashcards.front: A classmate says: 'Sound travels faster than light, because the thunder is so loud.' Which statement is correct?
A sound wave travels at 340 m/s with frequency 170 Hz. Calculate its wavelength.

items.answer: Wrong - light is far faster, so the flash arrives first and the thunder follows
